quests.title: The Warded Ledger
quests.directions: Given in prose by the giver and repeated in the journal. There is no marker of any kind on this quest and there is none anywhere in this build.

journal.text: Tesh says the ledger that would prove the gem-running is behind a warded door in the customs loft. She says it as if the door were weather.
There is more than one way at this. There always is; the trick is noticing the second one before you have used the first.
The ward comes apart like a knot and the hinge pins come off with it. The ledger is where she said, and the last four pages are in a different hand.
The undercustomer takes four hundred and turns his back for the length of a cigarette.
The collar-ward gives on the third pin. Nobody hears it.
The undercustomer is not paid enough to die for a loft. He does anyway.

resolutions.outcome: The ward comes apart like a knot and the hinge pins come off with it. The ledger is where she said, and the last four pages are in a different hand.
The undercustomer takes four hundred and turns his back for the length of a cigarette.
The collar-ward gives on the third pin. Nobody hears it.
The undercustomer is not paid enough to die for a loft. He does anyway.

The spring tide takes four metres off the bar for eleven minutes. I did not need a spell; I needed a table.
A Naga diver goes down for me and asks for nothing, which is worse.
